environments.description: Environments declared by this manifest, keyed by environment name.

exports.description: Services other applications may reach over private links.

imports.description: Services of other applications this application reaches.

jobs.description: One-shot jobs, run in declared order at their deployment point.

oneOf.description: Optional repository that supplies this application's manifest on Deploy.
Configuration shared by every preview.

routes.description: HTTP routes by hostname, activated on deployment.

secrets.description: Secrets whose values piqueld generates once per environment.

variables.description:
Default values of variables referenced as `${{ vars.<name> }}`, used by
environments that set no value of their own.

Build.description: Explicit build backend, extensible independently from source selection.

oneOf.description: Build a local container image using Docker.

args.description:
Values passed as `--build-arg`. They are recorded in image
metadata, so sensitive values belong in secrets instead.

context.description: Build context relative to the repository root.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path relative to the repository root.

oneOf.description: Multi-stage build target; the final stage when absent.

EnvironmentConfig.description:
Configuration of one environment, `[spec.environments.<name>]`, which
declares it (see [`super::declaration`]). Without `promote_from`, it builds
its own source: the saved manifest, or a branch of `spec.manifest`'s
repository. A block that sets none of `branch`, `commit`, `promote_from`
and `sync` leaves an existing environment's source as it is.

branch.description:
Branch of the manifest repository it follows; by default the one
`spec.manifest` names.

commit.description: Full commit it deploys instead of its branch's head.

promote_from.description:
Environment whose releases it receives, by `piquelctl env promote`,
instead of building.

sync.description:
Whether pushes to its branch deploy it while the repository syncs
(`spec.manifest.sync`); off when unset.

variables.description:
This environment's values: each overrides the `[spec.variables]` default
of the same name, or declares a variable without a default.

oneOf.description:
The strictest visibility this environment's routes get. The default,
`public`, restricts nothing; `private` keeps every route on the tailnet.

Export.description: A service other applications may reach, `[[spec.exports]]`.

applications.description: Applications whose environments may import the service.

previews.description:
Whether previews of those applications may import it too; `false` by
default, so only their environments can.

service.description: Service in this application that importers reach.

FileMode.description:
Octal file permissions from `0000` to `0777`, written as text such as
`"0444"` or `"644"`.

FileSource.description: Where a file's content comes from.

oneOf.description:
A file in the manifest's own repository, relative to its root, read at
the exact commit the manifest was fetched from. Only repository-backed
applications can use it.

path.description:
A file in the manifest's own repository, relative to its root, read at
the exact commit the manifest was fetched from. Only repository-backed
applications can use it.

oneOf.description: The content itself.

GitRepository.description: Git checkout configuration. Credentials come from the host's Git configuration.

branch.description: Branch to fetch when no commit is pinned.

url.description: Git clone URL or local repository path.

oneOf.description: HTTP health endpoint check.

retries.description: Consecutive failed probes that make the container unhealthy.

start_period_seconds.description: Startup grace in seconds, during which failed probes do not count.

oneOf.description: Executable command health check.

retries.description: Consecutive failed probes that make the container unhealthy.

start_period_seconds.description: Startup grace in seconds, during which failed probes do not count.

Import.description:
A service of another application this application reaches,
`[[spec.imports]]`, as `<service>.<application>`.

oneOf.description:
Environment of that application to reach. By default, the one named
like the importing environment. It may reference variables, so
previews can reach e.g. `staging`.

Job.description: A container that runs to completion at a defined point in each deployment.

command.description: Command replacing the service's command and arguments.

environment.description:
Environment variables only the job's container gets, added to its
service's. A name the service also sets is an error.

run.description: Deployment point at which the job runs.

secrets.description:
Secrets only the job's container mounts, added to its service's. A
target the service also mounts is an error.

service.description: Service whose prepared image, environment, secrets, and mounts the job reuses.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the job may run before the deployment fails.

volume_access.description: How the job may use the service's volumes.

JobRun.description: Deployment point at which a job runs.

JobVolumeAccess.description: How a job may use the volumes its service mounts.

ManifestRepository.description: The literal `"self"`, selecting the manifest's own repository.

Mount.description: A persistent volume mount in a service.

variables.description:
Values for every preview: each overrides the `[spec.variables]`
default of the same name, or declares a variable without a default.

oneOf.description:
The strictest visibility preview routes get; `private` by default, so
previews publish routes only with an explicit `public`.

preserve_path.description: Appends the request path and query to `to`.

RepositoryManifest.description: Independently selects the manifest that deployments, manual or on push, use.

path.description: Exact TOML or JSON file path relative to the repository root.

repository.description: Repository and revision containing the manifest.

sync.description:
How environments and previews follow pushes. Like the rest of
`spec.manifest`, ignored in fetched files.

RepositorySync.description:
How an application follows pushes to its manifest repository. Applies to
every preview, and to every environment following an unpinned branch that
opted in.

oneOf.description: Deploy only when asked.
List the branch heads every `interval_seconds`.
List the branch heads when GitHub reports a push.

ResourceLimits.description: Optional CPU and memory limits for a service.

oneOf.description: CPU limit in millicores.
Memory limit in bytes.

Rollout.description:
Optional `rollout` block of a service. Omitted fields keep their defaults,
so an empty block is equivalent to no block.

oneOf.description: Seconds Docker watches each replacement task for failure; 30 when omitted.
Update order; derived from the service's mounts when omitted.

Route.description:
HTTP route input, validated independently of ingress enablement.
A route sets either `service` and `port`, or `redirect`.

hostname.description:
Fully qualified DNS hostname, exact or a wildcard such as `*.example.com`
matching every name one label below `example.com`.

name.description:
Stable name, unique within the application, that selects this route in
every environment and preview, e.g. `piquelctl env url --route web`.
Declared after `hostname`, so routes stay ordered by hostname.

oneOf.description: Redirect answered by the gateway instead of a service.

visibility.description:
Who may connect; `private` (tailnet only) by default. Its environment's
ceiling can make it stricter, never looser.

SecretDeclaration.description:
A secret whose value piqueld generates for each environment when one of
its deployments first needs it. A generated value is never replaced, and
never shared with another environment.

name.description: Logical secret name; it cannot reference variables.

SecretEncoding.description: Text encoding of generated random bytes.

SecretGenerator.description: The exhaustive set of secret value generators.

oneOf.description: Random bytes from the operating system, encoded as text.

bytes.description: Number of random bytes before encoding.

encoding.description: Text encoding of the random bytes.

oneOf.description: RSA private key in PKCS#8 PEM.

SecretMount.description:
A secret exposed only as a container file. The name selects the
environment's generated secret when `spec.secrets` declares it, and the
application's store of manually set secrets otherwise.

name.description:
Logical secret name. It may reference variables, so each environment
can mount its own stored secret, e.g. `${{ vars.stripe_key }}`.

depends_on.description: Services in this application that must be healthy before this one rolls out.

files.description:
Read-only files mounted into the containers. Their contents are never
rendered with variables.

oneOf.description: Optional container health check.

receives_telemetry.description:
Whether the service receives the daemon's telemetry on the socket
directory mounted at `/run/piqueld/telemetry`, once its environment is
granted it. At most one service per application.

oneOf.description: Optional CPU and memory limits.

rollout.description: Optional rollout order and monitor window.

allOf.description: Where the file's content comes from.

mode.description: Octal permissions, `"0444"` by default. The file is owned by root.

target.description: Absolute, normalized container path of the file.

ServiceFile.description:
A read-only file mounted into a service's containers, from exactly one
source: `path` in the manifest's repository, or inline `content`.

Source.description: The exhaustive set of deployable service sources.

oneOf.description: Pull a prebuilt image from a registry.
Build a checked-out Git revision.

SourceRepository.description: The repository a Git build source checks out.

oneOf.description:
`"self"`: the application's manifest repository, at the exact commit its
manifest was read from, so one deployment builds from one revision.
An independently resolved repository and revision.

Template.description:
Text that may contain `${{ namespace.name }}` references, with optional
whitespace inside the braces. `$${{` writes a literal `${{`; `${VAR}` and
`$VAR` are ordinary text, left for shells and applications to expand.

```text
"${{ vars.domain }}"       -> the value of `domain`
"api.${{vars.domain}}"     -> "api." followed by the value of `domain`
"$${{ vars.domain }}"      -> "${{ vars.domain }}", literally
```

TypedTemplate.description: Schema of a template in a typed field: text containing `${{`.

Typed_RolloutOrder.description:
A typed value: a literal, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference yields the variable's own value;
any other template yields text. The result must then decode as `T`, so
strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description: Whether Docker stops a task before or after starting its replacement.
A value rendered from variables.

Typed_u16.description:
A typed value: a literal, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference yields the variable's own value;
any other template yields text. The result must then decode as `T`, so
strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description: A value rendered from variables.

Typed_u32.description:
A typed value: a literal, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference yields the variable's own value;
any other template yields text. The result must then decode as `T`, so
strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description: A value rendered from variables.

Typed_u64.description:
A typed value: a literal, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference yields the variable's own value;
any other template yields text. The result must then decode as `T`, so
strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description: A value rendered from variables.

Variable.description:
A declared variable value: a string, integer, or boolean. Strings may
reference system variables, but not other variables.

oneOf.description: A boolean.
A signed 64-bit integer.
Text, which may reference system variables.

Visibility.description:
Who may connect to a route: everyone, or only tailnet devices. It says
nothing about how traffic arrives; the installation decides that.

Variants are ordered from least to most restrictive, so the stricter of
two visibilities is their maximum.
